standardsBasis: IELTS Academic format (ielts.org); CEFR (Council of Europe); NGSL/AWL for vocabulary ordering. See docs/CONTENT_SOURCES.md.

cards.definitionEn: a thin amount of something spread over a surface
cards.example: A thin layer of ice covered the lake during the coldest week of winter.
cards.cloze: The report adds a new ___ of detail to earlier findings.
cards.confusables: level (a position in a system, not a sheet)

cards.definitionEn: a connection between two things or ideas
cards.example: Research shows a clear link between regular exercise and better memory in older adults.
cards.cloze: The study found a strong ___ between diet and heart disease.
cards.confusables: connection (similar, wider use)

cards.meaningVi: xác định vị trí, đặt tại
cards.definitionEn: to find the exact position of something
cards.example: Divers used sonar equipment to locate the wreck on the floor of the harbour.
cards.cloze: Engineers could not ___ the source of the leak.
cards.confusables: find (everyday word, less precise)

cards.definitionEn: to make something as great as possible
cards.example: Farmers plant early varieties to maximise yields before the dry season begins each year.
cards.cloze: Good lighting helps students ___ their concentration in class.
cards.confusables: increase (make bigger, not necessarily the most possible)

cards.definitionEn: small or not important compared with others
cards.example: The design needed only minor changes before the committee approved the final building plan.
cards.cloze: Only a ___ injury was reported after the accident.
cards.confusables: small (everyday word, no comparison implied)

cards.definitionEn: bad or harmful; less than zero
cards.example: Excessive screen time may have a negative effect on children's sleep and school performance.
cards.cloze: The results had a ___ impact on public confidence.
cards.confusables: harmful (only about damage, not about attitude or numbers)

cards.definitionEn: the final result of a process or event
cards.example: The outcome of the trial depended on evidence collected during the first investigation.
cards.cloze: No one could predict the ___ of the election.
cards.confusables: result (similar, more general)

cards.definitionEn: the study of knowledge, reality and values; a set of beliefs
cards.example: The school's philosophy places independent thinking above memorising facts for examinations each term.
cards.cloze: She studied ___ and politics at university.
cards.confusables: theory (a tested explanation, not a world view)

cards.meaningVi: thuộc về thể chất; thuộc vật lý
cards.definitionEn: relating to the body or to matter and energy
cards.example: Regular physical activity reduces the risk of heart disease in adults of all ages.
cards.cloze: The job requires ___ strength and good eyesight.
cards.confusables: mental (relating to the mind, the opposite area)

cards.definitionEn: a part of a whole, shown as a share or ratio
cards.example: A large proportion of the budget was spent on repairing roads after the floods.
cards.cloze: Only a small ___ of students live on campus.
cards.confusables: percentage (a proportion shown out of one hundred)

cards.definitionEn: to make writing available to the public
cards.example: The team will publish their findings in a leading journal later this year.
cards.cloze: They plan to ___ the report next month.
cards.confusables: print (produce copies, not release to the public)

cards.definitionEn: to behave in response to something
cards.example: Markets react quickly when governments announce unexpected changes to interest rates or taxes.
cards.cloze: How did the public ___ to the new law?
cards.confusables: respond (similar, often with words or planned action)

cards.definitionEn: to record a name or information on an official list
cards.example: Students must register for the examination before the end of the second teaching week.
cards.cloze: All visitors must ___ at the front desk.
cards.confusables: enrol (register for a course or school specifically)

cards.definitionEn: able to be trusted to work or behave well
cards.example: The new buses are more reliable and arrive on time even in heavy traffic.
cards.cloze: We need a ___ source of data for the study.
cards.confusables: trustworthy (mainly about people and their honesty)

cards.definitionEn: to depend on someone or something for support
cards.example: Remote villages rely on a single road for food deliveries during the winter months.
cards.cloze: Do not ___ on one source only for your essay.
cards.confusables: depend (similar, slightly less formal)

cards.definitionEn: to take something away from a place
cards.example: Workers remove plastic waste from the river before it reaches the sea each spring.
cards.cloze: Please ___ your shoes before entering the temple.
cards.confusables: delete (remove written or digital material)

cards.definitionEn: an official plan for achieving something
cards.example: The government scheme helps young families buy their first home at lower interest rates.
cards.cloze: The city launched a new recycling ___ last year.
cards.confusables: plan (similar, wider and less official)

cards.definitionEn: a series of things in a fixed order
cards.example: The sequence of events before the accident was recorded by cameras at the station.
cards.cloze: Follow the ___ of steps in the manual.
cards.confusables: series (a number of similar things, order less strict)

cards.definitionEn: the state of being male or female
cards.example: The survey recorded the age and sex of every participant before the analysis began.
cards.cloze: The form asks for your name, age and ___.
cards.confusables: gender (identity and social roles, a wider idea)

cards.meaningVi: sự thay đổi; ca làm; chuyển dịch
cards.definitionEn: a change in position, direction or emphasis
cards.example: There has been a clear shift towards online learning in universities in recent years.
cards.cloze: Public opinion began to ___ after the debate.
cards.confusables: change (similar, much wider meaning)

cards.meaningVi: nêu rõ, chỉ định cụ thể
cards.definitionEn: to state something clearly and in detail
cards.example: The contract must specify the exact date when the building work will be finished.
cards.cloze: Please ___ which size you require on the form.
cards.confusables: describe (give details, without fixing exact requirements)

cards.definitionEn: enough for a particular purpose
cards.example: The reservoir holds sufficient water to supply the town throughout the long dry season.
cards.cloze: There was not ___ evidence to charge the man.
cards.confusables: enough (the everyday word with the same meaning)

cards.meaningVi: nhiệm vụ, công việc được giao
cards.definitionEn: a piece of work that must be done
cards.example: The first task for the research team was to check samples from every site.
cards.cloze: Writing the report was a difficult ___.
cards.confusables: job (paid work, or any piece of work)

cards.definitionEn: relating to the practical use of machines or specialist knowledge
cards.example: The manual uses technical language that new engineers may find difficult to understand at first.
cards.cloze: The delay was caused by a ___ problem.
cards.confusables: technological (relating to technology as a field)

cards.meaningVi: kỹ thuật, phương pháp thực hành
cards.definitionEn: a skilled way of doing a practical activity
cards.example: Surgeons learn the technique by practising on models before they operate on real patients.
cards.cloze: The new ___ improved surgical results greatly.
cards.confusables: technology (machines and systems, not a personal skill)

cards.definitionEn: machines and systems developed from scientific knowledge
cards.example: Modern technology allows doctors to examine patients in distant villages without travelling there themselves.
cards.cloze: New ___ is changing the way we work.
cards.confusables: technique (a skilled method, not equipment)

cards.meaningVi: tính hợp lệ, giá trị đúng đắn
cards.definitionEn: the quality of being logically correct or legally acceptable
cards.example: Critics questioned the validity of the study because the sample was far too small.
cards.cloze: The court doubted the ___ of the contract.
cards.confusables: reliability (consistency of results, a different quality)

cards.definitionEn: the amount of something; the level of sound
cards.example: The volume of traffic through the port has doubled during the last ten years.
cards.cloze: The ___ of exports rose sharply this year.
cards.confusables: amount (similar, used for uncountable things generally)

cards.definitionEn: the right or ability to enter or use something
cards.example: Students have free access to the library catalogue from computers anywhere on the campus.
cards.cloze: You need a password to ___ the system.
cards.confusables: entry (physical entrance, not a right to use)

cards.meaningVi: sự đầy đủ, mức đáp ứng
cards.definitionEn: the quality of being enough or good enough
cards.example: Inspectors checked the adequacy of emergency exits in every public building in the district.
cards.cloze: The report questioned the ___ of the water supply.
cards.confusables: sufficiency (a similar formal noun, less common)

cards.definitionEn: happening once every year
cards.example: The annual report shows that membership of the sports club rose by ten percent.
cards.cloze: The festival is an ___ event held each spring.
cards.confusables: yearly (the everyday word with the same meaning)

cards.definitionEn: easy to see or understand; seeming to be true
cards.example: It soon became apparent that the bridge could not support heavy vehicles safely anymore.
cards.cloze: The damage was ___ from the photographs.
cards.confusables: obvious (stronger; impossible to miss)

cards.definitionEn: almost correct but not exact
cards.example: The approximate cost of the repairs was two thousand pounds, according to the engineer.
cards.cloze: Give the ___ number of visitors last year.
cards.confusables: exact (completely correct, the opposite)

cards.definitionEn: the way a person thinks or feels about something
cards.example: A positive attitude towards feedback helps students improve their writing much more quickly overall.
cards.cloze: Her ___ towards work changed after the course.
cards.wordFamily: attitudes (plural; attitudinal is rare and technical)
cards.confusables: opinion (a view on one question, not a general manner)

cards.definitionEn: to say that something was caused by something else
cards.example: Scientists attribute the decline in bee numbers to changes in farming methods and climate.
cards.cloze: He ___ his success to hard work.
cards.confusables: blame (attribute something bad, with disapproval)

cards.meaningVi: thuộc dân sự; thuộc công dân
cards.definitionEn: relating to citizens or to non-military life
cards.example: The new law protects the civil rights of every citizen, including freedom of speech.
cards.cloze: The dispute was settled in a ___ court.
cards.confusables: civic (relating to a city or town duties)

cards.definitionEn: a set of rules, symbols or secret letters
cards.example: All staff must follow the safety code when they work with chemicals in laboratories.
cards.cloze: Enter the ___ printed on your ticket.
cards.confusables: law (an official rule made by a government)

cards.definitionEn: to promise firmly; to do something wrong or illegal
cards.example: The council will commit more money to repairing schools over the next three years.
cards.cloze: The company refused to ___ to a fixed price.
cards.confusables: promise (the everyday word for giving your word)

cards.definitionEn: the exchange of information between people or groups
cards.example: Clear communication between doctors and patients reduces mistakes in hospitals, according to recent research.
cards.cloze: Good ___ is essential in a large team.
cards.confusables: conversation (spoken exchange only, usually informal)

cards.definitionEn: a large formal meeting for discussion
cards.example: Over three hundred researchers attended the conference on climate change held in Glasgow this autumn.
cards.cloze: She presented her paper at the ___.
cards.confusables: meeting (any gathering, usually smaller and less formal)

cards.definitionEn: a clear difference between two things being compared
cards.example: The report highlights the contrast between rural incomes and prices in the largest cities.
cards.cloze: In ___, the second village grew much faster.
cards.confusables: difference (any difference, not necessarily striking)

cards.definitionEn: a series of events that repeat in the same order
cards.example: The water cycle moves moisture from the oceans to the land and back again.
cards.cloze: The life ___ of the butterfly has four stages.
cards.confusables: circle (a round shape, not a repeating process)

cards.definitionEn: a formal discussion of opposing views
cards.example: The debate about university fees continued in parliament for several weeks during the spring.
cards.cloze: There is growing ___ about the new tax.
cards.confusables: argument (a disagreement, often angry and personal)

cards.definitionEn: without being affected by something; in spite of
cards.example: Despite the heavy rain, thousands of supporters attended the opening match of the season.
cards.cloze: ___ the cost, the plan went ahead.
cards.confusables: although (a conjunction followed by a clause, not a noun)

cards.definitionEn: a measurement of size; an aspect of something
cards.example: The architect measured every dimension of the old building before drawing the restoration plans.
cards.cloze: Cost is another ___ of the problem.
cards.confusables: size (overall largeness, everyday word)

cards.definitionEn: relating to one's own country or to home life
cards.example: Domestic flights are cheaper than international ones, but trains are often faster between cities.
cards.cloze: The airline only operates ___ flights.
cards.confusables: internal (inside an organisation or country, more formal)

cards.definitionEn: to appear or become known after being hidden
cards.example: New evidence may emerge when the committee publishes its full report later this year.
cards.cloze: Problems ___ when funding was cut suddenly.
cards.confusables: appear (the everyday word, without the idea of becoming known)

cards.definitionEn: a mistake in action, judgement or calculation
cards.example: The report contained a serious error in the figures for the final quarter.
cards.cloze: The accident was caused by human ___.
cards.confusables: mistake (the everyday word with the same meaning)

cards.definitionEn: relating to a group with shared culture and origin
cards.example: The city is home to many ethnic communities, each with its own festivals and food.
cards.cloze: The museum celebrates the ___ diversity of the region.
cards.confusables: racial (relating to race, a narrower and sensitive term)

cards.definitionEn: something you aim to achieve
cards.example: The main goal of the programme is to train nurses for hospitals in rural areas.
cards.cloze: Her ___ is to study medicine abroad.
cards.wordFamily: goals (plural; goalkeeper is a sports compound)
cards.confusables: aim (similar, often slightly less fixed)

cards.meaningVi: khoản tài trợ; cấp, ban cho
cards.definitionEn: money given by an organisation for a special purpose
cards.example: The university received a research grant to study coastal erosion over the next five years.
cards.cloze: She applied for a ___ to fund her study.
cards.confusables: fund (money generally, or to provide money)

cards.definitionEn: for this reason; therefore
cards.example: The road was closed after the storm; hence, all buses were diverted through smaller villages.
cards.cloze: He missed the deadline; ___, his application failed.
cards.confusables: therefore (similar, more common in writing)

cards.definitionEn: an idea that is tested through research
cards.example: The experiment was designed to test the hypothesis that sleep improves memory in students.
cards.cloze: The data did not support their ___.
cards.confusables: theory (an explanation supported by much evidence)

cards.definitionEn: to put a plan or system into action
cards.example: Schools need time and funding to implement the new curriculum successfully across all regions.
cards.cloze: The city will ___ the scheme in January.
cards.confusables: apply (use a rule or method, not carry out a whole plan)

cards.meaningVi: liên quan, dính líu (vào việc sai)
cards.definitionEn: to show that someone is involved in something wrong
cards.example: The documents implicate two senior officials in the decision to hide the true costs.
cards.cloze: The evidence may ___ other members of staff.
cards.confusables: involve (take part, without suggesting wrongdoing)

cards.meaningVi: áp đặt, áp dụng (thuế, hạn chế)
cards.definitionEn: to force a rule or tax on people
cards.example: The government may impose a tax on sugary drinks to reduce childhood obesity rates.
cards.cloze: The council decided to ___ a parking charge.
cards.confusables: force (make someone do something, wider meaning)

cards.definitionEn: to combine parts into a whole; to mix socially
cards.example: The course aims to integrate theory with practical experience in local schools and hospitals.
cards.cloze: New staff ___ quickly into the existing team.
cards.confusables: combine (join things together, no social sense)

cards.definitionEn: inside an organisation, country or body
cards.example: The internal report criticised delays in the hospital building project over the past year.
cards.cloze: This is an ___ matter for the company.
cards.confusables: domestic (relating to a country or home, not an organisation)

cards.definitionEn: to examine something carefully to find the truth
cards.example: Police will investigate the cause of the fire that destroyed the warehouse last night.
cards.cloze: Scientists are ___ why the species is declining.
cards.confusables: research (study a subject generally, not one event)

cards.definitionEn: paid work that someone does for an employer
cards.example: Many graduates take a part-time job while they search for work in their field.
cards.cloze: She applied for a new ___ at the hospital.
cards.wordFamily: jobs (plural; jobless is a derived adjective)
cards.confusables: work (activity in general, uncountable)

cards.definitionEn: a small piece of material giving information about something
cards.example: Every bottle carries a label showing its ingredients, weight and the date of production.
cards.cloze: Check the ___ before you wash this jacket.
cards.confusables: tag (a small label, often for a price)

cards.definitionEn: a system of parts that work together; a method
cards.example: The body has a natural mechanism for controlling temperature during exercise in hot weather.
cards.cloze: The report describes the ___ behind the decision.
cards.wordFamily: mechanisms (plural; mechanical is a related adjective)
cards.confusables: system (a whole set of connected things, wider)

cards.definitionEn: easy to see or understand
cards.example: It was obvious from the results that the new method saved both time and money.
cards.cloze: The answer should be ___ to any reader.
cards.confusables: apparent (clear after looking, slightly weaker)

cards.definitionEn: to fill or use a space or time
cards.example: The new offices occupy the top three floors of the tallest building in the centre.

cards.confusables: fill (put something into a space, everyday word)

cards.definitionEn: something that can be chosen
cards.example: For many students, sharing a flat is the cheapest option near the university campus.
cards.cloze: We have no ___ but to delay the trip.
cards.confusables: choice (the act of choosing, or the thing chosen)

cards.definitionEn: the amount of something produced by a person or machine
cards.example: Factory output rose sharply after the company installed faster machines on the production line.
cards.cloze: The plant increased its ___ by twenty percent.
cards.confusables: production (the process of making things)

cards.definitionEn: including everything; in general
cards.example: The overall standard of the essays was high, although a few needed clearer structure.
cards.cloze: The ___ results were better than expected.
cards.confusables: general (usual or widespread, less about totals)

cards.definitionEn: side by side and the same distance apart; similar
cards.example: The new cycle path runs parallel to the river for almost ten kilometres through town.
cards.cloze: The two roads run ___ to each other.
cards.confusables: similar (alike, without the idea of lines or matching development)

cards.meaningVi: thông số; giới hạn quy định
cards.definitionEn: a fact or limit that controls how something is done
cards.example: The study measured several parameters, including temperature, rainfall and the speed of the wind.
cards.cloze: Work within the ___ set by the manager.
cards.confusables: limit (the highest possible level, everyday word)

cards.definitionEn: a stage in the development of something
cards.example: The first phase of the housing project will provide homes for two hundred families.
cards.cloze: The plan is still in its early ___.
cards.confusables: stage (similar, often one part of a process)

cards.definitionEn: to say what will happen in the future
cards.example: Experts predict that sea levels will rise steadily along the coast during this century.
cards.cloze: It is hard to ___ the final result.
cards.confusables: forecast (predict weather or economic figures, using data)

cards.definitionEn: most important; main
cards.example: The principal reason for the delay was a shortage of trained staff during winter.
cards.cloze: Cost is the ___ concern for most buyers.
cards.confusables: principle (a rule or belief; a noun with different spelling)

cards.definitionEn: happening or existing before something else
cards.example: Applicants need prior experience of working with children before they can join the programme.
cards.cloze: No ___ knowledge of the subject is required.
cards.confusables: previous (similar, more common and less formal)

cards.definitionEn: relating to a job needing special training; a trained person
cards.example: The museum offers professional training for teachers who want to use its collections in class.
cards.cloze: She gave the team ___ advice on the design.
cards.confusables: expert (a person with deep knowledge, not necessarily by job)

cards.definitionEn: a planned piece of work with a clear aim
cards.example: The project to rebuild the station will take three years and employ six hundred workers.
cards.cloze: The ___ was finished ahead of schedule.
cards.wordFamily: projects (plural; projection is a related technical noun)
cards.confusables: plan (the details thought out before the work)

cards.meaningVi: thúc đẩy, quảng bá; thăng chức
cards.definitionEn: to encourage something; to move someone to a higher job
cards.example: The campaign aims to promote cycling as a cheap and healthy way to travel.
cards.cloze: Posters ___ the new museum exhibition.
cards.confusables: advertise (tell the public about a product, for payment)

cards.meaningVi: chế độ (chính trị); chế độ sinh hoạt
cards.definitionEn: a system of government; a planned programme of activity
cards.example: Under the new regime, local councils gained control over schools and transport in the region.
cards.cloze: He follows a strict exercise ___.
cards.wordFamily: regimes (plural; regimen is a related medical word)
cards.confusables: government (the group of people who rule a country)

cards.definitionEn: to find a solution to a problem or disagreement
cards.example: The two companies met last week to resolve their disagreement over the price of materials.
cards.cloze: Talks helped to ___ the dispute quickly.
cards.confusables: solve (find the answer to a problem or puzzle)

cards.definitionEn: to keep or continue to have something
cards.example: Old forests retain water in their soil and reduce flooding in valleys after heavy rain.
cards.cloze: The club works hard to ___ its best players.
cards.confusables: keep (the everyday word with the same meaning)

cards.definitionEn: a number of similar things happening one after another
cards.example: The university will host a series of lectures on ocean science during the spring term.
cards.cloze: The book is the first in a ___.
cards.wordFamily: series (same form in singular and plural)
cards.confusables: sequence (things in a fixed order, one after another)

cards.definitionEn: a number that gives information about something
cards.example: One striking statistic shows that cycling injuries fell after the new lanes were built.
cards.cloze: The report quotes a ___ about unemployment.
cards.confusables: figure (a number, everyday word)

cards.definitionEn: the position of someone or something in society or a system
cards.example: The wetland gained protected status after scientists recorded rare birds breeding there in spring.
cards.cloze: Check the ___ of your application online.
cards.confusables: position (place or rank, everyday word)

cards.meaningVi: căng thẳng; áp lực; nhấn mạnh
cards.definitionEn: great pressure or worry; emphasis on a word
cards.example: Long working hours are a common cause of stress among hospital staff in winter.
cards.cloze: The teacher placed ___ on careful pronunciation.
cards.confusables: pressure (demands that cause worry, often from work)

cards.definitionEn: happening after something else
cards.example: The first study was small, but subsequent research confirmed its main findings with larger samples.
cards.cloze: The results appeared in a ___ report.
cards.confusables: later (the everyday word with the same meaning)

cards.definitionEn: the total of numbers added together; an amount of money
cards.example: The charity raised a large sum of money to rebuild homes destroyed by the earthquake.
cards.cloze: He paid a large ___ for the old house.
cards.confusables: total (the final amount, adjective or noun)

cards.definitionEn: a short account of the main points of something
cards.example: At the end of the lecture, the professor gave a brief summary of the main arguments.
cards.cloze: Write a short ___ of the passage.
cards.confusables: outline (the main points, without details of content)

cards.definitionEn: to start doing something that needs effort
cards.example: The team will undertake a full survey of the island's plants during the dry season.
cards.cloze: Few firms will ___ such a risky project.
cards.confusables: carry out (do a task, less formal)

cards.definitionEn: a school or society for special study or training
cards.example: She trained as a dancer at the national academy before joining a company in London.
cards.cloze: He teaches history at a military ___.
cards.confusables: institute (an organisation for research or training)

cards.definitionEn: to change something slightly; to get used to conditions
cards.example: Drivers should adjust their speed when fog reduces visibility on the motorway at night.
cards.cloze: You can ___ the height of the chair.
cards.confusables: adapt (change yourself or something for new conditions)

cards.definitionEn: to change something, usually slightly
cards.example: The designers had to alter the plans after the council rejected the original roof design.
cards.cloze: Nothing could ___ the final decision.
cards.confusables: change (the general word for making different)

cards.definitionEn: to change a law or document slightly to improve it
cards.example: Parliament voted to amend the law so that small firms pay less tax each year.
cards.cloze: The committee agreed to ___ the draft report.
cards.confusables: revise (change a text or plan, wider use)

cards.definitionEn: knowing about something and understanding it
cards.example: Most drivers are aware of the dangers of using a phone while driving in cities.
cards.cloze: Were you ___ of the new rules?
cards.confusables: conscious (aware, often of feelings or surroundings)

cards.definitionEn: the maximum amount something can hold; the ability to do something
cards.example: The new stadium has a seating capacity of sixty thousand for international football matches.
cards.cloze: The theatre has a ___ of five hundred.
cards.confusables: ability (the power to do something, about people)

cards.definitionEn: a difficult task or situation that tests ability
cards.example: Reducing carbon emissions is the greatest challenge facing governments in every industrial country today.
cards.cloze: The mountain presented a serious ___ to climbers.
cards.confusables: problem (something that must be solved, not a test)

cards.definitionEn: a section of a legal document; part of a sentence
cards.example: One clause in the contract allows either side to end the agreement with written notice.
cards.cloze: Read the final ___ of the contract carefully.
cards.confusables: term (a condition of an agreement, everyday word)

cards.definitionEn: a substance made from two or more elements
cards.example: Water is a chemical compound made of hydrogen and oxygen in fixed proportions.
cards.cloze: The lab tested a new carbon ___.
cards.wordFamily: compounds (plural; compounding is a technical verb form)
cards.confusables: mixture (substances mixed but not chemically joined)

cards.definitionEn: a serious disagreement or fight between people or groups
cards.example: The conflict between the two departments over funding slowed the whole building programme considerably.
cards.cloze: The plan caused ___ between staff and managers.
cards.confusables: dispute (a disagreement, often official and less violent)

cards.definitionEn: to ask for advice or information from someone
cards.example: Before making a decision, managers should consult staff who will be affected by the changes.
cards.cloze: You should ___ a doctor if pain continues.
cards.confusables: ask (the everyday word for requesting information)

cards.definitionEn: communication with someone; touch between things
cards.example: Students in remote areas stay in contact with their teachers through weekly video calls.
cards.cloze: Please ___ the office if you cannot attend.
cards.confusables: communication (the exchange of information in general)

cards.definitionEn: to become smaller or weaker; to refuse politely
cards.example: Sales of printed newspapers continue to decline as more readers move to online news.
cards.cloze: Birth rates ___ in many developed countries.
cards.confusables: decrease (become less, the neutral word)

cards.definitionEn: separate and distinct from others
cards.example: The course is divided into three discrete modules, each ending with its own examination.
cards.cloze: The data falls into two ___ groups.
cards.confusables: separate (apart from others, everyday word)

cards.definitionEn: a first version of a piece of writing
cards.example: The first draft of the report was too long, so the team shortened several sections.
cards.cloze: She wrote a ___ of the essay in pencil.
cards.confusables: version (any form of something, not only early ones)

cards.definitionEn: to make it possible for someone to do something
cards.example: New software will enable doctors to share patient records securely between different hospitals in seconds.
cards.cloze: The grant will ___ the school to buy equipment.
cards.confusables: allow (give permission, everyday word)

cards.definitionEn: the power that makes machines work and bodies move
cards.example: Solar panels convert sunlight into energy that can power homes throughout the whole year.
cards.cloze: Wind is a growing source of clean ___.
cards.confusables: power (energy in use, or control over people)

cards.definitionEn: to make people obey a rule or law
cards.example: Traffic police enforce speed limits strictly on the road that passes the village school.
cards.cloze: It is hard to ___ the ban in villages.
cards.confusables: impose (introduce a rule or tax, not make people obey)

cards.definitionEn: something that exists separately, such as an organisation
